references.text: Isaiah was commissioned to preach to a people with sluggish hearts who would not understand – a parallel to Jesus’ rebuke of the disciples who were "slow of heart" to believe ([ref:Jes 6:9-10|Isaiah 6:9-10]).

Ezekiel speaks of a people who have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear – an expression of spiritual sluggishness that recalls Jesus’ words to the disciples ([ref:Esek 12:2|Ezekiel 12:2]).

Right after rebuking them, Jesus explained that the Messiah had to suffer these things and enter into his glory, and he interpreted for them what was written about him in all the Scriptures – this emphasizes that the prophets truly spoke of all these things ([ref:Luk 24:26-27|Luke 24:26-27]).

Later, Jesus opened the disciples’ minds so they could understand the Scriptures, and showed that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled – they needed this opening precisely because they had been slow to believe ([ref:Luk 24:44-45|Luke 24:44-45]).

Paul testifies that he says nothing other than what the prophets and Moses said would happen: that the Messiah should suffer and, as the first, rise from the dead – exactly what the disciples were slow to believe ([ref:Apg 26:22-23|Acts 26:22-23]).

Isaiah’s prophecy about the suffering servant whom no one believed the message of – the prophets had clearly spoken of the Messiah’s suffering, but it was hard to believe ([ref:Jes 53:1-3|Isaiah 53:1-3]).
Moses prophesied about a prophet like himself whom the Lord would raise up – a foundational messianic prophecy that the disciples should have believed ([ref:5 Mos 18:15-19|Deuteronomy 18:15-19]).
Paul calls the Galatians "foolish" (anoētoi) – the same Greek word Jesus uses here – because they did not hold fast to the gospel of the crucified Christ ([ref:Gal 3:1-3|Galatians 3:1-3]).

Jesus predicted his suffering, death, and resurrection to the disciples, but they did not understand this saying and were afraid to ask him – an example of the sluggishness Jesus rebukes in Luke 24:25 ([ref:Mark 9:31-32|Mark 9:31-32]).

Peter writes that the prophets searched and explored the salvation they prophesied about, seeking to find out what time or circumstances the Spirit of Christ in them pointed to when it foretold Christ’s sufferings and the glory that would follow – thus the prophets truly spoke of these things ([ref:1 Pet 1:10-11|1 Peter 1:10-11]).
